extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and others interested in USPTO practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: This document is a USPTO Final Order approving an affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent and cites the specific USPTO disciplinary rules and procedural regulations implicated by the respondent's conduct. It is a model of how the Office describes alleged violations, examples of misconduct, and the procedures and consequences for resignation and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a disciplinary rule the OED Director believes was violated. In this matter, the Office identified conduct such as allowing patent applications to go abandoned without client knowledge as illustrative of prejudicial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglecting a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director alleged the respondent neglected five patent applications (allowing them to go abandoned) and failed to apprise himself of their status; these factual examples show what constitutes neglect under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b) via 10.23(c)(8) — failing to timely inform a client of Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to timely inform a client of correspondence received from the Office when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) was received by the practitioner on behalf of a client, and (iii) was correspondence of which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the respondent's failure to update the client on the status of five applications and not accurately responding to a client's status request as examples of this violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — engaging in dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is included among those the OED Director opined were violated; the Order references the respondent presenting multiple payments that were dishonored as related misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (parallel provision in the Rules of Professional Conduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited alongside other misconduct rules; the Order treats failure to manage client matters and respond to disciplinary requests as conduct prejudicial to justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — failing to act with thoroughness and preparation reasonably necessary for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with the thoroughness and preparation reasonably necessary for the representation of a client; failing to do so is a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director asserted the respondent failed to keep up with the status of five patent applications and failed to keep client informed, illustrating a lack of required thoroughness and preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client; failure to do so is sanctionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the Order include allowing applications to be abandoned, not responding to client inquiries, and submitting payments that were dishonored.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3)-(a)(4) — failing to keep client reasonably informed and to comply with requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the respondent's failure to update the client on five patent applications and not accurately responding to a client's status request as examples of breaches of these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) — failing to cooperate with OED or respond to lawful demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in an investigation of any matter before it, or knowingly failing to respond to a lawful demand or request for information from a disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order alleges the respondent failed to respond to OED's lawful requests for information; noncooperation with OED is separately cited as a ground for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 — affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rule governing submission and approval of an Affidavit of Resignation to obtain exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director determined the respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complied with 11.27(a) and therefore approved the affidavit and ordered exclusion on consent. The Order itself is issued pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — obligations of an excluded practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements a person excluded from practice before the USPTO must follow (respondent shall comply with § 11.58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly requires the respondent to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the text does not restate the subsection but makes compliance a condition of the exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 — OED Director obligations upon exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural obligations of the OED Director in connection with accepted resignations and exclusions (e.g., publication requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director is ordered to comply with § 11.59 and to publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and a notice materially consistent with the provided text in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 — reinstatement application and conclusive presumption for limited purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing applications for reinstatement after exclusion; the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining reinstatement, that the allegations set forth in the disciplinary proceeding are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged awareness of § 11.60 and that if and when he applies for reinstatement the OED Director will apply the stated presumption. This affects how reinstatement applications are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 — statutory authority for discipline and exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory authority under which the USPTO Director may approve resignations and exclude practitioners from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states these statutory provisions as the legal basis for approving the affidavit of resignation and excluding the respondent on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct constituting violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific factual examples the OED Director relied upon: allowing five patent applications to go abandoned without the client's knowledge or consent; failing to apprise himself of the status of the five patent applications; presenting multiple payments to the Office that were dishonored; failing to update the client on the status of the client's five patent applications and accurately respond to the client's request for a status update; failing to keep the mailing address updated in the patent applications; and failing to respond to OED's lawful requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete behaviors are presented as illustrative evidence of breaches of the cited rules (neglect, lack of diligence, failure to inform clients, possible misrepresentation, and failure to cooperate with disciplinary authorities). They serve as practical indicators of the cited rule violations.
